title: Add authoritative inventory wear/doff state owner
description: PR #455 review had to fail closed for every held blocksDoff item because inventory.location is free-form storage prose and cannot prove whether an item is donned. Add a closed, semantic wear-state owner and model-facing don/doff transition that preserves source curse onset/persistence, then narrow the conservative custody gate without allowing synonyms or raw state writes to bypass it.
design: Do not infer wear from arbitrary inventory.location. Keep held storage, world placement, wear state, attunement, and character curse state separate. Curse attachment must outlive item placement where the source requires it.
acceptance_criteria: Wear state is first-class and migration-safe; don/doff is a semantic atomic mutation; blocksDoff and don-triggered curse onset are source-faithful; ambiguous legacy placement fails closed; ordinary held-but-not-worn items remain transferable; full lifecycle and importer/runtime tests pass.
notes:
Dispatch plan (attempt 1, 2026-07-19, supervisor eshyra-fe3t): Codex gpt-5.6-luna in .worktrees/eshyra-mq4n branch eshyra-mq4n off eshyra-fe3t (includes stbg, dunv migration 0019, 2n1t.8.1 migration 0020). Your schema change must be migration 0021; update migrationLegacyAdoption ledger/applied pins and regenerate schema.snapshot.sql (npx tsx packages/core/scripts/generate-schema-snapshot.ts). Keep wear state separate from held storage (inventory.location free text), world placement (world_location_id), attunement, and character curse state; blocksDoff gating currently fails closed for every held item — narrow it to don/doff semantics without synonym inference. Sources of truth for curse onset/persistence: the magic-item records' curse/attunement fields (Demon Armor, Berserker Axe, Armor of Vulnerability, Shield of Missile Attraction, Robe of the Archmagi, Orb of Dragonkind).
Completion report (2026-07-19): Added migration 0021_inventory_wear_state and regenerated schema.snapshot.sql. Added authoritative inventoryWear donItem/doffItem/getInventoryWearState owner with exact model-facing don_item/doff_item tools; legacy rows without wear state fail closed for don/doff. New give/claim/reacquire/adoption rows initialize not_worn; relinquishment removes holder wear state; transfer moves state to recipient as not_worn. Narrowed blocksDoff custody gating to explicitly worn items, preserving held-not-worn transfer/removal semantics. Don attaches source-defined don-onset curse state to character conditions so it survives doff/placement. Tests added/updated for lifecycle, migration, registry, and conservative custody behavior. Verification: npm run build passed; focused suites passed (138 tests); full npm test had 4620 passed, with remaining failures caused by sandbox EPERM for child-process/loopback operations (git/node/npm spawn and 127.0.0.1 listen). npm run verify:worktree reached format then failed at check:hidden-unicode for the same sandbox spawnSync git EPERM. No follow-up product issues discovered.
Supervisor review round 1 (2026-07-19) — two blocking findings; fix in the same worktree (attempt 2), tree is uncommitted:
F1 (major, fail-open): assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady now treats a MISSING inventory_wear_state row as not-worn, so an unreviewed legacy held blocksDoff item (e.g. pre-migration Demon Armor, worn in fiction) can be dropped/sold/transferred where the previous code failed closed. Required: for a held item whose record declares curse.blocksDoff, a missing wear row is AMBIGUOUS and must fail closed (same message family as before), while an authoritative not_worn row permits custody. Missing-row ambiguity is resolved only by the adoption/repair boundary that seeds authoritative rows.
F2 (major, crash): removeItem partial-quantity relinquish inserts an inventory_wear_state row for the NEW unheld relinquished row, bound to the FORMER holder — violating the 'wear row exists iff held' invariant — and claimItem/reacquireItem then do a plain INSERT into inventory_wear_state for that id, which hits the PRIMARY KEY and throws a raw SqliteError: any claim/reacquire of a partially-dropped/sold stack is permanently broken. Required: do not create wear rows for unheld rows (drop the partial-path INSERT); keep full-relinquish DELETE; make claim/reacquire seeding collision-safe (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(inventory_id) DO UPDATE SET character_id, wear_state='not_worn', ...) so surviving rows are rebound not fatal.
Also add regression tests: claim after partial drop; reacquire after partial sell; legacy blocksDoff held item with no wear row fails closed for dropped/sold/lost/transfer/doff; invariant sweep that every inventory_wear_state row joins to a held inventory row with matching character_id (assert in relevant lifecycle tests).
Completion report (attempt 2, 2026-07-19): Fixed supervisor F1 by making held blocksDoff custody fail closed when inventory_wear_state is missing or bound to a different holder; authoritative not_worn remains allowed. Fixed F2 by removing the partial-relinquishment wear-row insert and making claim/reacquire wear seeding collision-safe upserts that rebind to the new holder and reset to not_worn. Made transfer wear maintenance the same upsert so the invariant is preserved for legacy held rows too. Added regressions for missing-row dropped/sold/lost/doff/transfer custody, claim after partial drop, reacquire after partial sell, and invariant sweeps ensuring every wear row joins a held inventory row with matching character_id. Verification: focused requested suites passed (6 files, 174 tests): domainMutations.test.ts, inventoryWear.test.ts, itemTransfer.test.ts, itemAdoption.test.ts, tools.test.ts, migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts. npm run typecheck passed; git diff --check passed. Bead intentionally left open for supervisor verification/merge.
Supervisor: attempt-2 F1/F2 fixes re-verified in code (fail-closed ambiguity gate; wear-row-iff-held invariant; upserts at claim/reacquire/transfer). Full verify:worktree green. Committed and merged into eshyra-fe3t.
